title: Escalation Play Compiler: bundle telemetry + runbooks for PD/Slack incidents
creator: Neha Patel
description:
Problem: When an alert fires for latency or error spikes we frequently lack a concise, actionable bundle of telemetry and playbook steps attached to the PagerDuty incident or Slack thread. Currently responders must manually pull traces, SLO deltas, and the right runbook fragments which increases MTTR and leads to repeated context switching.

Goal: Build an 'Escalation Play Compiler' service that, given an alert/incident event, compiles a deterministic artifact containing: a one-paragraph incident summary, top 3 related traces (snippets and links), metric deltas & SLO impact, recent deploys, and the most relevant runbook steps. The artifact should be attached to PagerDuty incidents and posted into the originating Slack channel as a compact thread starter. The compiler also emits a postmortem seed (title, timeline bullets, implicated services) to reduce friction when creating postmortems.
acceptance_criteria:
- Compiler generates artifact for at least 3 alert types (latency P99 spike, 5xx error burst, cache KV-miss storm)
- Artifact contains: summary paragraph, up to 3 trace links/snippets, SLO delta (%), top metric graphs links, last deploy info, and 2 runbook action items
- Artifact is attached to PagerDuty incident via PD API and posted to Slack channel within 30s of incident creation for test alerts
- Postmortem seed created in /postmortems folder with prefilled title and implicated services tag
- End-to-end integration covered by end-to-end test harness and smoke tests
- Security review completed and KMS-access patterns documented
technical_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- We'll base trace selection on a scoring heuristic (error weight + latency delta + trace duration) to avoid heavy fan-out.
- To limit runtime cost, the compiler will fetch up to 50s of trace/search context and then run scoring; heavy aggregation will be async for longer incidents.
- Runbook fragments are stored as small markdown blocks in the Runbook index service; mapping uses tag similarity (service, symptom) + statically curated fallbacks.
- We will avoid embedding full spans in messages; only include 1-2 short span snippets and links to full traces in Traces UI for security and payload size reasons.
- PagerDuty attachments use PD notes API; Slack uses message blocks with a single collapsed details block to reduce noise.
- Security: the compiler will redact PII and cluster internal tokens, and call KMS for any secrets. Security review required (see security_review_required).
rollout_plan:
1) Feature branch with unit tests and local mock PD/Slack connectors (R&D). 2) Canary: route compiler for alerts from observability-dev namespace only (2% traffic) for 1 week. 3) Expand to staging alerts and runbook authoring flow. 4) Gradual ramp to production 25/50/100% after SLA smoke tests. 5) Monitor false-positive attachments and user feedback for 2 weeks, then iterate.
- Rollout flags: feature.compiler.enabled, compiler.attach_pd, compiler.post_to_slack
test_plan:
- Unit tests for trace scoring heuristic and runbook mapping.
- Integration tests using observability-test-cluster that simulate latency spike and 5xx bursts; assert artifact creation and content shape.
- E2E smoke that triggers an alert and asserts PD note attached and Slack thread posted within 30s.
- Load test to ensure compiler can handle 200 incidents/min with 95th latency under 1s for artifact generation (mocked downstreams).
- Manual security verification and redaction tests by Security team.
